language is a doorway to a country’s people, its history and its heart. for many learners in india, the sinhala language of sri lanka is a doorway that has remained closed, not because the language is impossible to learn, but because there are so few books with which to open it. a new learner who looks for a sinhala grammar book in an indian bookshop, or searches for one on the internet, finds very little. there are a few phrase lists and some scattered notes, but hardly anything that explains sinhala grammar (සිංහල ව්යාකරණ) step by step for a beginner who comes from an indian-language background. this shortage makes the first steps unnecessarily difficult, and many learners lose heart before they have properly begun. this book is my attempt to fill that gap. i have planned it as a guide for absolute beginners, moving slowly from the very basics towards advanced grammar. every topic is explained in simple english and simple sinhala, and hindi meanings are given with the examples so that the learner can link the new language with one that is already familiar. each lesson contains many examples, tables and diagrams, and ends with practice questions so that learners can check their own progress. in preparing this book i have taken the help of an ai tool, together with the knowledge that i have acquired while studying sinhala. an ai tool is only a helper; it is not the final authority on a language. there may therefore be some mistakes in spelling, in grammar rules or in the wording of examples. i request every reader, and especially teachers and native speakers of sinhala, to double-check the contents carefully before relying on them. corrections and suggestions of any kind are most welcome, and they will be used to improve the book in later editions. i sincerely hope that this work will be a useful companion for new learners and will make the beautiful sinhala language a little easier to approach. khem chetry november 2026

1.1 what is grammar? (ව්යාකරණය යනු කුමක්ද?) every language works by rules, even when nobody has written them down. grammar is the study of those rules: how sounds make words, how words change their form, and how words are arranged into sentences. in sinhala the word for grammar is ව්යාකරණය (vyaakaranaya). it comes from the sanskrit word vyākaraṇa (व्याकरण), meaning “to explain in detail”, so hindi uses exactly the same word. ව්යාකරණය යනු භාෂාවක නීති රීති පිළිබඳ ශාස්ත්රයයි. vyaakaranaya yanu bhaashaawaka neethi reethi pilibanda shaasthrayayi. grammar is the science of the rules of a language. व्याकරण किसी भाषा के नियमों का शास्त्र है। think of road signs. a driver who ignores the signs may still reach the destination, but with danger and confusion. grammar gives the language its road signs: it tells the speaker and the listener the same thing, so that nobody is lost. grammar is not meant to make a language hard. it is meant to make it clear. ව්යාකරණ දැනුමෙන් භාෂාව නිවැරදිව කතා කිරීමට සහ ලිවීමට හැකි වේ. vyaakarana daenumen bhaashaawa niwaradiwa kathaa kireemata saha liweemata haeki we. with a knowledge of grammar one can speak and write the language correctly. व्याकरण के ज्ञान से भाषा को सही ढंग से बोला और लिखा जा सकता है। why learn grammar? — five benefits # sinhala english hindi 1 නිවැරදිව කතා කිරීම niwaradiwa kathaa kireema to speak correctly सही बोलना 2 නිවැරදිව ලිවීම niwaradiwa liweema to write correctly सही लिखना 3 හොඳින් තේරුම් ගැනීම hondin theerum gaeneema to understand well अच्छी तरह समझना 4 පරිවර්තනය කිරීම pariwarthanaya kireema to translate अनुवाद करना 5 විභාග සහ නිල කටයුතු wibhaaga saha nila katayuthu for examinations and official work परीक्षा और सरकारी कामकाज के लिए

1.4 building blocks of language (භාෂාවේ මූලික ඒකක) ශබ්ද එකතු වී අක්ෂර වේ; අක්ෂර එකතු වී පද වේ; පද එකතු වී වාක්ය වේ. shabda ekathu wee akshara we; akshara ekathu wee pada we; pada ekathu wee waakya we. sounds join to become letters; letters join to become words; words join to become sentences. ध्वनियाँ मिलकर अक्षर बनती हैं; अक्षर मिलकर शब्द बनते हैं; शब्द मिलकर वाक्य बनते हैं। ශබ්දය sound ध्वनि → අක්ෂරය letter अक्षर → පදය word शब्द → වාක්යය sentence वाक्य → ඡේදය paragraph अनुच्छेद → රචනාව essay निबंध follow one example from the smallest block to the largest: block example sound (ශබ්දය) the sound “ma” letter (අක්ෂරය) ම word (පදය) මම — “i” mama sentence (වාක්යය) මම යනවා. — “i go.” mama yanawa. paragraph (ඡේදය) three to six sentences about one idea essay (රචනාව) several paragraphs about one topic in this book you will climb this ladder step by step: letters in lessons 2–3, words in lessons 4–24, sentences in lessons 25–27 and paragraphs, essays and letters in lessons 31–32.

1.8 translation tips (පරිවර්තන උපදෙස්) පරිවර්තනයේදී ක්රියා පදය අවසානයට දමන්න. pariwarthanayedee kriyaa padaya awasaanayata damanna. in translation, put the verb at the end. अनुवाद में क्रिया को अंत में रखें। # tip english → sinhala note 1 put the verb last i read a book. → මම පොතක් කියවනවා. english s-v-o becomes s-o-v 2 drop “the”; “a” becomes an ending the book → පොත a book → පොතක් things take -ක් 3 people take a different ending for “a” a teacher → ගුරුවරයෙක් a child → ළමයෙක් people take -ෙක් 4 english small words become endings to school → පාසලට from school → පාසලෙන් of me → මගේ ට = to, ෙන් = from, ගේ = of 5 question: add ද to the key word are you a teacher? ඔබ ගුරුවරයෙක්ද? ද = question marker 6 negative: use නැහැ i do not go. මම යන්නේ නැහැ. නැහැ = no / not 7 if you think in hindi, the order is already right मैं किताब पढ़ता हूँ → මම පොත කියවනවා both are s-o-v worked examples: # english sinhala hindi 1 we go to school. අපි පාසලට යනවා. api paasalata yanawa. हम स्कूल जाते हैं। 2 he drinks tea. ඔහු තේ බොනවා. ohu thee bonawa. वह चाय पीता है। 3 she reads a letter. ඇය ලිපියක් කියවනවා. aeya lipiyak kiyawanawa. वह एक पत्र पढ़ती है। 4 are you a teacher? ඔබ ගුරුවරයෙක්ද? oba guruwarayekda? क्या आप शिक्षक हैं? 5 i do not go. මම යන්නේ නැහැ. mama yanne naehae. मैं नहीं जाता/जाती। 6 the students write the lesson. සිසුවෝ පාඩම ලියනවා. sisuwo paadama liyanawa. विद्यार्थी पाठ लिखते हैं। sinhala into english: # sinhala english hindi 1 මම කඳවුරට යනවා. mama kandawurata yanawa. i go to the camp. मैं शिविर जाता/जाती हूँ। 2 තාත්තා ගමට යනවා. thaaththaa gamata yanawa. father goes to the village. पिताजी गाँव जाते हैं। 3 ඔවුන් සිංහල කතා කරනවා. owun sinhala kathaa karanawa. they speak sinhala. वे सिंहली बोलते हैं। tip — method to translate sinhala into english: (1) find the verb at the end, (2) find who does it (the subject), (3) find what it is done to (the object), (4) read the small endings (ට, ෙන්, ගේ) and then build the english sentence.

1.10 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these eight points 1. grammar (ව්යාකරණය) is the science of the rules of a language. 2. sinhala belongs to the indo-aryan family, like hindi. 3. grammar has four branches: sounds, word forms, sentences, meaning. 4. sound → letter → word → sentence → paragraph → essay. 5. a basic sentence has subject (උක්තය), object (කර්මය) and verb (ක්රියාව). 6. the sinhala order is s – o – v; the verb comes last, as in hindi. 7. spoken sinhala and written sinhala differ, mainly in verb endings and vocabulary. 8. when translating, put the verb last and turn english small words into endings (ට, ෙන්, ගේ).

Lesson 2: Sinhala Sounds and the Alphabet

lesson 2 lesson 2: sinhala sounds and the alphabet සිංහල අක්ෂරමාලාව सिंहली ध्वनियाँ और वर्णमाला key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the difference between a sound and a letter 2. how the sinhala script is written (abugida) 3. the 18 vowels (ස්වර) with their hindi partners 4. the special signs ං, ඃ and ් 5. the 41 consonants (ව්යඤ්ජන) in their five groups 6. pronunciation tips for hindi speakers

2.1 sounds and letters (ශබ්ද සහ අක්ෂර) අපි කථා කරන්නේ ශබ්ද වලිනි. අපි ලියන්නේ අක්ෂර වලිනි. api kathaa karanne shabda walini. api liyanne akshara walini. we speak with sounds. we write with letters. हम ध्वनियों से बोलते हैं। हम अक्षरों से लिखते हैं। the full set of letters of a language is its alphabet. in sinhala it is called අක්ෂරමාලාව (aksharamaalaawa, “the garland of letters”) or හෝඩිය (hoodiya). hindi calls it वर्णमाला. five facts about the sinhala script will save you much trouble: left to right. sinhala is written from left to right, like english and hindi. no capital letters. there is no difference between “big” and “small” letters. names such as කොළඹ (colombo) are written like any other word. no headline. hindi letters hang from a line (शिरोरेखा); sinhala letters do not. they are round and written freely. an abugida. a consonant letter already carries the vowel “a”: ක is ka, not just k. to change the vowel we add a sign (lesson 3). one letter, one sound. sinhala spelling is regular: each letter has one sound, so once you know the alphabet you can read any word.

2.2 the vowels (ස්වර) a vowel (ස්වරය, hindi: स्वर) can be spoken by itself. the traditional alphabet has 18 vowels. they come in short and long pairs. a short vowel is called හ්රස්ව (hrasva, short) and a long vowel දීර්ඝ (diirgha, long). hindi uses the same two words: ह्रस्व and दीर्घ. letter roman hindi example word english hindi type අ a अ අම්මා ammaa mother माँ short ආ aa आ ආච්චි aachchi grandmother दादी / नानी long ඇ ae — ඇස aesa eye आँख short ඈ aae — ඈත aaetha far दूर long ඉ i इ ඉර ira sun सूरज short ඊ ii ई ඊයේ iiye yesterday बीता कल long උ u उ උදේ ude morning सुबह short ඌ uu ऊ ඌරා uuraa pig सूअर long ඍ ru ऋ ඍෂි rishi sage ऋषि short (sanskrit) ඎ ruu ॠ — very rare अति दुर्लभ long (sanskrit) ඏ lu ऌ — very rare अति दुर्लभ short (sanskrit) ඐ luu ॡ — very rare अति दुर्लभ long (sanskrit) එ e ए එක eka one एक short ඒ ee ए ඒක eeka that (thing) वह long ඓ ai ऐ ඓතිහාසික aithihaasika historical ऐतिहासिक diphthong ඔ o ओ ඔරලෝසුව oraloosuwa clock, watch घड़ी short ඕ oo ओ ඕනෑ oonae want, need चाहिए long ඖ au औ ඖෂධ aushadha medicine दवा diphthong rule — how to remember the vowels • ten everyday vowels: අ ආ ඇ ඈ ඉ ඊ උ ඌ එ ඒ ඔ ඕ (twelve, counting the pairs) – learn these first. • two diphthongs (two vowel sounds joined): ඓ = a + i, ඖ = a + u. • four sanskrit vowels: ඍ ඎ ඏ ඐ. only ඍ is seen, in a few sanskrit words such as ඍෂි. hindi-speakers know ऋ already. • sinhala has the two vowels ඇ and ඈ, which hindi has no letter for. say them like the “a” in the english word cat. tip — short “e” and “o” hindi has only one ए and one ओ. sinhala has two of each: short එ, ඔ and long ඒ, ඕ. listen: එක (eka, one) is quick; ඒක (eeka, that) is held longer.

2.3 three special signs (විශේෂ ලකුණු) sign name what it does example hindi partner ං බිංදුව bindduwa adds a nasal sound (ng / m) සිංහල – sinhala sinhala ं (अनुस्वार) ඃ විසර්ගය visargaya a breath “ha” after a vowel; only in sanskrit words දුඃඛය – sorrow duhkhaya ः (विसर्ग) ් හල් කිරීම hal kireema removes the vowel “a”; the letter is now a pure consonant බත් – cooked rice bath ् (हलन्त / विराम) look at the third sign. ක is ka. when we put ් on it, ක් is only k. words may end in such a letter: බත් (bath, rice), ගස් (gas, trees), පොත් (poth, books). this sign also helps us make plurals (lesson 7). remember — ං or ඞ? the sign ං is a “dot” (බිංදුව) added to a vowel or consonant. the letter ඞ is a full consonant of the ක group. do not mix them up.

2.4 the consonants (ව්යඤ්ජන) a consonant (ව්යඤ්ජනය, hindi: व्यंजन) needs a vowel to be spoken. the traditional alphabet has 41 consonants. the first 25 are arranged in five groups by the place in the mouth where the tongue or lips touch. hindi arranges its first 25 consonants in the same way, so a hindi-speaker already knows the plan! group 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 5th (nasal) කණ්ඨජ velar (throat) कण्ठ्य ක ka क ඛ kha ख ග ga ग ඝ gha घ ඞ nga ङ තාලුජ palatal (palate) तालव्य ච cha च ඡ chha छ ජ ja ज ඣ jha झ ඤ nya ञ මූර්ධජ retroflex (tongue curled) मूर्धन्य ට ṭa ट ඨ ṭha ठ ඩ ḍa ड ඪ ḍha ढ ණ ṇa ण දන්තජ dental (teeth) दन्त्य ත ta त ථ tha थ ද da द ධ dha ध න na न ඕෂ්ඨජ labial (lips) ओष्ठ्य ප pa प ඵ pha फ බ ba ब භ bha भ ම ma म in this chart ත ථ ද ධ න (dental) are written ta tha da dha na, and ට ඨ ඩ ඪ ණ (retroflex) are written with a dot below. in running text of this book, the plain letters “th” and “t” are used for ත and ට; see the pronunciation key. after the 25 come the remaining consonants: kind letters (sinhala · roman · hindi) අන්තස්ථ anthastha – semi-vowels अन्तःस्थ ය ya य ර ra र ල la ल ව wa व ඌෂ්ම uushma – sibilants and breath ऊष्म ශ sha श ෂ sha ष ස sa स හ ha ह විශේෂ visesha – special विशेष ළ ḷa ळ ෆ fa फ़ ඥ gna ज्ञ prenasalised nasal + stop sounds पूर्वानुनासिक ඟ nga ङ्ग ඦ nja ञ्ज ඬ ṇḍa ण्ड ඳ nda न्द ඹ mba म्ब key idea — count the letters 25 (five groups) + 4 (ය ර ල ව) + 4 (ශ ෂ ස හ) + ළ + ෆ + ඥ + 5 prenasalised = 41 consonants. 18 vowels + 41 consonants = 59 letters. everyday modern sinhala uses fewer of them; the rest appear mostly in words from sanskrit, pali and foreign languages.

2.5 pronunciation tips for hindi speakers letters tip example ඛ ඝ ඡ ඣ ඨ ඪ ථ ධ ඵ භ these “aspirated” letters are still written, but in modern spoken sinhala they are not breathed out. say ඛ like ක and ඵ like ප. do not say ख or फ with a puff of breath! ඵලය palaya (not “phalaya”) – result फल ට ත ඩ ද retroflex and dental pairs sound almost the same in speech. spelling must be learned by looking at words. තාත්තා father पिता ටැංකිය tank टंकी ඇ ඈ open the mouth wide, as for the “a” in cat. hindi has no letter for this sound. ඇය she वह (स्त्री) aeya ඹ ඳ ඟ ඬ a very light nasal sound is heard before the stop: ඹ is mb, ඳ is nd. අඹ mango आम සඳ moon चाँद ළ a soft “l” with the tongue curled back, as ळ in marathi. කළු black काला kalu ශ ෂ ස all three are said close to “s” or “sh” by most speakers. learn the spelling of each word. ශිෂ්යයා student शिष्य shishyayaa tip — study tip for hindi speakers learn sinhala letters in the same order as your hindi varnamala: ක ඛ ග ඝ ඞ — क ख ग घ ङ. say both aloud, one pair at a time. within a week you will know the 25 letters of the five groups.

2.8 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. sinhala is written left to right, has no capital letters, and each consonant carries the vowel “a”. 2. there are 18 vowels in the traditional alphabet: short, long, and two diphthongs (ඓ, ඖ). 3. there are 41 consonants; the first 25 are in five groups, just as in hindi. 4. ං adds a nasal sound; ඃ adds a breath; ් removes the vowel. 5. aspirated letters (ඛ, ඝ, ඵ …) are written but not breathed out in modern speech. 6. ඇ and ඈ have no hindi letters; say them like the “a” in cat.

2.10 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 18 vowels and 41 consonants sections 2.2 and 2.4 2 ආ, ඊ, ඌ, ඒ, ඕ short and long pairs 3 ඓ (ऐ) and ඖ (औ) diphthongs 4 क, ग, त, प, म, स same order as hindi 5 ච = palatal; ට = retroflex; ත = dental; ප = labial; ක = velar five groups 6 ඟ, ඦ, ඬ, ඳ, ඹ section 2.4 7 ඛ, ඵ, ඝ the second and fourth letter of a group 8 (a) අඹ (b) සඳ (c) ඉර section 2.6 9 it removes the vowel “a”; ක් (hindi: हलन्त) section 2.3 10 a nasal sound (ng / m); සිංහල section 2.3 tip — coming next lesson 3: vowel signs and conjunct letters (පිළි). you will learn how a vowel is written on a consonant (කා, කි, කු …), and how two consonants join in one letter (ක්ර, ක්ෂ, ම්බ …).
Lesson 3: Vowel Signs and Conjunct Letters

lesson 3 lesson 3: vowel signs and conjunct letters පිළි සහ සංයුක්ත අක්ෂර मात्राएँ और संयुक्ताक्षर key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what a vowel sign (පිල්ල) is and where it is written 2. the 14 vowel signs with the letter ක 3. the complete syllable chart for four consonants 4. the special signs for ර and ය (්ර, ්ය, ර්) 5. double and joined consonants (ක්ක, ම්ම, ක්ෂ) 6. read 12 words and avoid common spelling errors

3.1 what is a vowel sign? (පිළි) ව්යඤ්ජනයකට ස්වරයක් එක් කරන්නේ පිල්ලකිනි. wyanjanayakata swarayak ek karanne pillakini. a vowel is added to a consonant by a vowel sign. व्यंजन में स्वर मात्रा से जुड़ता है। you know that ක carries the vowel “a”. to say kaa, ki or ku we do not write a new letter. we keep the consonant and add a small mark called a පිල්ල (pilla, plural පිළි, pili). hindi calls it मात्रा. the idea is the same, and many shapes are different. the vowel signs are written before, after, above, below or on both sides of the consonant: position signs examples with ක before the letter ෙ ේ ෛ කෙ කේ කෛ after the letter ා ැ ෑ කා කැ කෑ above the letter ි ී කි කී below the letter ු ූ ෘ කු කූ කෘ on both sides ො ෝ ෞ කො කෝ කෞ tip — same as hindi hindi also has a sign that goes in front (ि in कि) and signs above and below (े, ु). sinhala follows the same idea, but the signs look different.

3.2 the vowel signs with ක letter roman hindi example word english hindi ක ka क කඩය kadaya shop दुकान කා kaa का කාසිය kaasiya coin सिक्का කැ kae — කැඩපත kaedapatha mirror दर्पण කෑ kaae — කෑම kaaema food, meal भोजन කි ki कि කිරි kiri milk दूध කී kii की කීයද? kiiyada how much? कितना? කු ku कु කුරුල්ලා kurullaa bird चिड़िया කූ kuu कू කූඩුව kuuduwa cage, nest पिंजरा, घोंसला කෘ kru कृ කෘෂිකර්මය krushikarmaya agriculture कृषि කෙ ke के කෙසෙල් kesel banana केला කේ kee के කේක් keek cake केक කො ko को කොළ kola leaf पत्ता කෝ koo को කෝපි koopi coffee कॉफ़ी කෛ kai कै — rare दुर्लभ කෞ kau कौ කෞතුකාගාරය kauthukaagaaraya museum संग्रहालय names of some signs. ා is the ඇලපිල්ල (aelapilla); ි is the ඉස්පිල්ල (ispilla); ු is the පාපිල්ල (paapilla); ෘ is the ගැටපිල්ල (gaetapilla); ෙ is the කොම්බුව (kombuwa); ෞ is the ගයනුකිත්ත (gayanukitta). long ී ූ ේ are the “long” forms of ි ු ෙ. your teacher may use other names for ැ and ෑ. remember — two shapes, one sound ො and ෝ look like ෙ + ා. they are written as one sign around the consonant. never write ෙ and ා as two separate things.

3.4  Letters for ර and ය  (රකාරාංශය, යංශය, රේඵය)

3.4 letters for ර and ය (රකාරාංශය, යංශය, රේඵය) the letters ර and ය can join a consonant in a short form. there are three such forms, and you will meet them in many words, including the word ව්යාකරණ itself. name form example english hindi රකාරාංශය rakaaraamshaya ක්ර ක්රියාව kriyaawa action, verb क्रिया රකාරාංශය rakaaraamshaya ප්ර ප්රශ්නය prashnaya question प्रश्न යංශය yamshaya ව්ය ව්යාකරණය wyaakaranaya grammar व्याकरण යංශය yamshaya ෂ්ය ශිෂ්යයා shishyayaa student शिष्य යංශය yamshaya ත්ය සත්යය sathyaya truth सत्य රේඵය repaya ර්ම කර්මය karmaya object (grammar), deed कर्म රේඵය repaya ර්ථ අර්ථය arthaya meaning अर्थ රේඵය repaya ර්ව සර්වනාමය sarwanaamaya pronoun सर्वनाम key idea — good news for hindi speakers many words in this table are the same in hindi: क्रिया, प्रश्न, व्याकरण, अर्थ, सर्वनाम. if you can spell the hindi word, you can usually predict the sinhala spelling.

3.5 double and joined consonants (සංයුක්ත අක්ෂර) when two consonants come together with no vowel between them, the first one takes the sign ් (hal), and often the two letters are written close together or joined. the commonest joined pair is a double consonant: double word english hindi ක්ක අක්කා akkaa older sister बड़ी बहन / दीदी ම්ම අම්මා ammaa mother माँ ත්ත තාත්තා thaaththaa father पिता ල්ල මල්ලි malli younger brother छोटा भाई ය්ය අයියා ayyaa older brother बड़ा भाई / भैया ච්චි ආච්චි aachchi grandmother दादी / नानी two different consonants can join too: joined letters word english hindi ස්ව ස්වරය swaraya vowel स्वर න්ධ සන්ධිය sandhiya joining (of sounds) सन्धि ම්බ අම්බරය ambaraya sky आकाश ස්ත්ර ශාස්ත්රය shaasthraya science, scripture शास्त्र ක්ෂ ක්ෂේත්රය kshethraya field क्षेत्र ක්රී ක්රීඩාව kriidaawa sport, game खेल

3.6 read aloud # sinhala english hindi 1 පොත potha book किताब 2 මල mala flower फूल 3 ගස gasa tree पेड़ 4 පාසල paasala school स्कूल 5 නිවස niwasa house घर 6 ළමයා lamayaa child बच्चा 7 ගුරුවරයා guruwarayaa teacher शिक्षक 8 ශිෂ්යයා shishyayaa student विद्यार्थी 9 කෑම kaaema food भोजन 10 කිරි kiri milk दूध 11 ක්රීඩාව kriidaawa sport खेल 12 ප්රශ්නය prashnaya question प्रश्न

3.7 common spelling mistakes # mistake advice 1 confusing ඉ / ඊ and උ / ඌ short sound = no extra length; long sound = held. check each word in a dictionary at first. 2 confusing ණ / න and ල / ළ they sound alike. learn the spelling with the word, e.g. කළු (black), නිවස (house). 3 confusing ශ / ෂ / ස learn the spelling with the word, e.g. ශිෂ්යයා, සිංහල, ගුරුවරයා. 4 writing ෙ after the letter ෙ ේ ෛ always come before the letter. 5 forgetting ් (hal) a final consonant needs ් (hal): බත් (rice), ගස් (trees). always check the end of the word. 6 splitting ක්ර, ව්ය, ශ්ර these are joined forms. type or write them as one unit.

3.8 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 පිල්ල / පිළි pilla / pili vowel sign(s) मात्रा(एँ) 2 සංයුක්ත අක්ෂර samyuktha akshara joined letters संयुक्ताक्षर 3 රකාරාංශය rakaaraamshaya sign for ර joined below रकार चिह्न 4 යංශය yamshaya sign for ය joined below यकार चिह्न 5 රේඵය repaya sign ර් written above रेफ 6 අක්කා akkaa older sister दीदी 7 අයියා ayyaa older brother भैया 8 මල්ලි malli younger brother छोटा भाई 9 නංගි nangi younger sister छोटी बहन 10 තාත්තා thaaththaa father पिता 11 අම්මා ammaa mother माँ 12 ආච්චි aachchi grandmother दादी / नानी

3.9 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. a vowel sign (පිල්ල) changes the vowel of a consonant: ක + ා = කා. 2. ෙ ේ ෛ go before; ා ැ ෑ after; ි ී above; ු ූ ෘ below; ො ෝ ෞ on both sides. 3. ්ර (රකාරාංශය) and ්ය (යංශය) are short forms of ර and ය joined below a letter; ර් (රේඵය) goes above. 4. double consonants such as ක්ක, ම්ම, ත්ත are very common: අක්කා, අම්මා, තාත්තා. 5. many spellings are the same as in hindi: ක්රියා, ප්රශ්න, ව්යාකරණ.

3.10 practice questions (අභ්යාස) part a: vowel signs q1. add the signs and write the syllable: ග + ා, ම + ි, ත + ු, ස + ෙ, ප + ො. q2. which signs are written before the consonant? q3. which sign goes on both sides of the consonant? part b: joined letters q4. name the sign used in (a) ක්රියා (b) ව්යාකරණ (c) කර්ම. q5. write in sinhala: mother, father, older sister, grandmother. q6. write the hindi word for: ප්රශ්නය, අර්ථය, ශාස්ත්රය. part c: reading and spelling q7. write in roman letters: කිරි, කෑම, පාසල. q8. write in sinhala: book, flower, tree, village. q9. correct the mistake: (a) ෙක (for කෙ) (b) බත (for “rice”). explain. q10. make a sentence with three words from the read aloud list, and translate it into english and hindi.

3.11 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 ගා, මි, තු, සෙ, පො section 3.2 2 ෙ, ේ, ෛ written before the letter 3 ො, ෝ, ෞ written around the letter 4 (a) රකාරාංශය (b) යංශය (c) රේඵය section 3.4 5 අම්මා, තාත්තා, අක්කා, ආච්චි section 3.5 6 प्रश्न, अर्थ, शास्त्र same words in hindi 7 kiri, kaaema, paasala section 3.2 8 පොත, මල, ගස, ගම section 3.6 9 (a) කෙ (b) බත්; ෙ is written before the letter; the end consonant needs ් (hal) section 3.7 10 example: ළමයා කිරි බොනවා. the child drinks milk. बच्चा दूध पीता है। verb last tip — coming next lesson 4: words and syllables (පද). you will learn how syllables make words, where sinhala words come from, and how words are built from a root and endings.

lesson 4 lesson 4: words and syllables පද සහ අක්ෂර शब्द और अक्षर key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. syllables (අක්ෂර) and how to count them 2. the four kinds of sinhala words by origin 3. the sanskrit–sinhala–hindi connection 4. root + ending: how a word is built 5. compound words (සමාස පද) 6. word families built on one root

4.1 syllables (අක්ෂර) වචනයක් කොටස් වලට බෙදා කියන්නට පුළුවන්. wachanayak kotas walata bedaa kiyannata puluwan. a word can be divided into parts when we speak it. किसी शब्द को बोलते समय भागों में बाँटा जा सकता है। a word is made of one or more syllables, the beats you hear when you say it slowly. in sinhala writing, one letter with its vowel sign is usually one syllable. to count syllables, clap once for each beat. # word syllables count english · hindi 1 පොත potha පො – ත 2 book · किताब 2 ගම gama ග – ම 2 village · गाँव 3 ළමයා lamayaa ළ – ම – යා 3 child · बच्चा 4 පාසල paasala පා – ස – ල 3 school · स्कूल 5 ශිෂ්යයා shishyayaa ශි – ෂ්ය – යා 3 student · विद्यार्थी 6 ක්රීඩාව kriidaawa ක්රී – ඩා – ව 3 sport · खेल 7 ගුරුවරයා guruwarayaa ගු – රු – ව – ර – යා 5 teacher · शिक्षक 8 ව්යාකරණය wyaakaranaya ව්යා – ක – ර – ණ – ය 5 grammar · व्याकरण tip — why syllables matter in lesson 5 onwards you will add endings to words (ළමයා + ට = ළමයාට). knowing where one syllable ends and the next begins helps you add the ending without spelling mistakes.
4.2  Kinds of Words by Origin  (පද වර්ග)

4.2 kinds of words by origin (පද වර්ග) sinhala has borrowed words from many sources over two thousand years. traditional grammar sorts them into four kinds. hindi grammar uses almost the same classification, so you can compare them: kind meaning sinhala examples hindi name තත්සම thathsama the same as the original sanskrit or pali word ජලය (water) පුත්රයා (son) ගුරු (teacher) මිත්රයා (friend) तत्सम තද්භව thadbhawa a changed (worn-down) form of the sanskrit word ගම (village) අත (hand) කන (ear) ඇස (eye) तद्भव දේශීය desiiya a native word of the island අම්මා (mother) මල්ලි (younger brother) ගෙදර (home) देशज විදේශීය widesiiya borrowed from foreign languages බස් (bus) පාන් (bread) කමිසය (shirt) ජනේලය (window) බොත්තම (button) विदेशी the words පාන්, කමිසය, ජනේලය and බොත්තම came from portuguese, which sri lanka met in the 16th century; බස් came from english.
4.3  Sanskrit, Sinhala and Hindi: One Family

4.3 sanskrit, sinhala and hindi: one family both sinhala and hindi grew out of the sanskrit family of languages. often the sinhala word and the hindi word are cousins: they come from the same sanskrit word, and each has changed in its own way. compare: # sanskrit sinhala hindi english 1 ग्राम (gramam) ගම gama गाँव village 2 हस्त (hasta) අත atha हाथ hand 3 कर्ण (karna) කන kana कान ear 4 अक्षि (akshi) ඇස aesa आँख eye 5 दन्त (danta) දත datha दाँत tooth 6 अग्नि (agni) ගින්න ginna आग fire 7 रात्रि (ratri) රෑ raae रात night 8 मत्स्य (matsya) මාළු maalu मछली fish key idea — a learner’s trick when you meet a new sinhala word, ask: “is there a hindi word that sounds a little like this?” if the answer is yes, the word is probably easy to remember. if no, learn it as a new word.

4.4 root and ending (මූල සහ ප්රත්ය) a word often has a root (the main part) and an ending (a small part added at the end). in sinhala, endings do many jobs: they show a, “to”, “from”, “of”, and the tense of a verb. look at these: # root + ending = word meaning 1 පොත potha + ක් පොතක් pothak a book 2 ළමයා lamayaa + ට ළමයාට lamayaata to the child 3 ගම gama + ට ගමට gamata to the village 4 ගම gama + ෙන් ගමෙන් gamen from the village 5 ළමයා lamayaa + ගේ ළමයාගේ lamayaage of the child 6 පොත potha + ෙහි පොතෙහි pothehi in the book 7 යන yana + වා යනවා yanawaa goes / go 8 කියවන kiyawana + වා කියවනවා kiyawanawaa reads / read endings like -ට, -ෙන්, -ගේ and -ෙහි belong to the cases (විභක්ති), which you will study in detail in part iii. for now, notice that sinhala adds endings to a word, where english adds small words like “to”, “from” and “of”.

4.5 compound words (සමාස පද) two words may join to make one new word. this is a සමාස පදය (samaasa padaya, compound word). hindi also has समास. # compound parts english hindi 1 රජමාළිගාව rajamaaligaawa රජ (king) + මාළිගාව (palace) royal palace राजमहल 2 පොත්හල pothhala පොත් (books) + හල (hall) bookshop पुस्तक की दुकान 3 මහපාර mahapaara මහ (great) + පාර (road) main road मुख्य सड़क 4 සූර්යෝදය suuryoodaya සූර්ය (sun) + උදය (rising) sunrise सूर्योदय 5 සති අන්තය sathi anthaya සති (week) + අන්තය (end) weekend सप्ताहांत

4.6 word families many sinhala words are built from one root. learning a root gives you several words at once. here is the root for “write”: # word english hindi 1 ලියනවා liyanawaa writes लिखता है 2 ලිවීම liweema writing (the act) लिखना / लेखन 3 ලිපිය lipiya letter पत्र 4 ලේඛකයා lekhakayaa writer लेखक 5 ලේඛනය lekhanaya document, writing लेख / दस्तावेज़ a second family is built on learn (ඉගෙන ගන්නවා, igena gannawaa): ඉගෙනීම (learning), ඉගැන්වීම (teaching), උගත් (educated), ශිෂ්යයා (student). add your own families as you read.

4.8 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. a syllable is one beat of a word; ළමයා has three (ළ – ම – යා). 2. words are of four kinds by origin: තත්සම, තද්භව, දේශීය, විදේශීය (hindi: तत्सम, तद्भव, देशज, विदेशी). 3. many sinhala and hindi words are cousins from the same sanskrit word: ගම / गाँव, අත / हाथ. 4. a word has a root and an ending: ගම + ට = ගමට. 5. two words can join as a compound (සමාස): රජ + මාළිගාව = රජමාළිගාව.

lesson 5 lesson 5: nouns නාම පද संज्ञा key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what a noun (නාම පදය) is 2. the five kinds of nouns 3. living (සජීවී) and non-living (අජීවී) nouns 4. noun endings and the sinhala “a / one” (-ක්)

5.1 what is a noun? (නාම පදය) පුද්ගලයෙකුගේ, සතෙකුගේ, දෙයක නමට නාම පදය යැයි කියනවා. puddgalayekuge, sathekuge, deyaka namata naama padaya yaeyi kiyanawaa. the name of a person, an animal or a thing is a noun. व्यक्ति, प्राणी या वस्तु के नाम को संज्ञा कहते हैं। a noun (නාම පදය, hindi: संज्ञा) names a person (ගුරුවරයා), a place (කොළඹ), an animal (කුරුල්ලා), a thing (පොත) or an idea (සතුට). in a sentence a noun is usually the subject or the object. # sinhala english hindi 1 ගුරුවරයා පොතක් කියවනවා. guruwarayaa pothak kiyawanawaa the teacher reads a book. शिक्षक किताब पढ़ता है। 2 කුරුල්ලා ගසේ ඉන්නවා. kurullaa gase innawaa the bird is in the tree. चिड़िया पेड़ पर है। 3 කොළඹ ලොකු නගරයක්. kolaba loku nagarayak colombo is a big city. कोलंबो एक बड़ा शहर है।

5.2 the five kinds of nouns kind meaning sinhala examples hindi common සාමාන්ය නාම a name for any one of a class ළමයා (child), පොත (book), ගස (tree), පාසල (school) जातिवाचक proper විශේෂ නාම the special name of one person or place කොළඹ (colombo), මහනුවර (kandy), ශ්රී ලංකාව (sri lanka) व्यक्तिवाचक collective සමූහ නාම a group taken as one පන්තිය (class), හමුදාව (army), පවුල (family), රැළ (herd) समूहवाचक material ද්රව්ය නාම a substance රත්තරන් (gold), යකඩ (iron), වතුර (water), කිරි (milk) द्रव्यवाचक abstract භාව නාම a quality, feeling or idea that you cannot touch සතුට (joy), දුක (sorrow), ධෛර්යය (courage), විනය (discipline), ආදරය (love) भाववाचक tip — compare with hindi hindi and sinhala share the five kinds. but take care: words that look alike can differ in meaning. ආදරය means love, while hindi आदर means respect.

5.3 living and non-living nouns (සජීවී / අජීවී) this division is very important in sinhala. it changes the verb “to be”, the plural and the case endings: class examples verb “is / are / has” living (සජීවී) sajiivi – people, animals ළමයා, ගුරුවරයා, බල්ලා, කුරුල්ලා ඉන්නවා (inna-waa) – “is, lives, stays” non-living (අජීවී) ajiivi – things, plants, places පොත, ගස, ගෙදර, වතුර තියෙනවා (thiyenawaa) – “is, exists, has” # sinhala english hindi 1 ගුරුවරයා පන්තියේ ඉන්නවා. guruwarayaa panthiye innawaa the teacher is in the class. शिक्षक कक्षा में है। 2 පොත මේසය උඩ තියෙනවා. potha mesaya uda thiyenawaa the book is on the table. किताब मेज़ पर है। 3 බල්ලා ගෙදර ඉන්නවා. ballaa gedara innawaa the dog is at home. कुत्ता घर पर है। 4 ගසේ මල් තියෙනවා. gase mal thiyenawaa there are flowers on the tree. पेड़ पर फूल हैं। remember — never mix them “පොත ඉන්නවා” is wrong, and “ගුරුවරයා තියෙනවා” is wrong. ask: is it alive? then use ඉන්නවා. if not, use තියෙනවා.

5.4 noun endings most sinhala nouns end in one of the vowels below. knowing the ending helps you add the endings of the cases (part iii). ends in examples note අ (short a) පොත (book), ගස (tree), ගම (village), මල (flower) mostly things ආ (long aa) ළමයා (child), අම්මා (mother), ගුරුවරයා (teacher) mostly living beings ඉ / උ කිරි (milk), මල්ලි (younger brother), ගුරු (teacher), කළු a few ය / ව මේසය (table), කාමරය (room), පුටුව (chair), කතාව (story) things; the ය / ව often drops in the plural

5.5 “a” and “one”: the ending -ක් sinhala has no word for “the” or “a”. a bare noun can mean “the book” or just “book”. to say “a / one”, we add -ක් to things and -ෙක් to people: # noun “a / one …” english hindi 1 පොත potha පොතක් pothak a book एक किताब 2 ගස gasa ගසක් gasak a tree एक पेड़ 3 මල mala මලක් malak a flower एक फूल 4 ගම gama ගමක් gamak a village एक गाँव 5 පාසල paasala පාසලක් paasalak a school एक स्कूल 6 ගෙදර gedara ගෙදරක් gedarak a house एक घर 7 ළමයා lamayaa ළමයෙක් lamayek a child एक बच्चा 8 ගුරුවරයා guruwarayaa ගුරුවරයෙක් guruwarayek a teacher एक शिक्षक 9 මිනිසා minisaa මිනිසෙක් minisek a man एक आदमी 10 කුරුල්ලා kurullaa කුරුල්ලෙක් kurullek a bird एक चिड़िया rule — rule things: word + ක් (පොත → පොතක්) people and animals: drop the final ආ, add ෙක් (ළමයා → ළමයෙක්)

5.6 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 නාම පදය naama padaya noun संज्ञा 2 සාමාන්ය නාමය saamaanya naamaya common noun जातिवाचक संज्ञा 3 විශේෂ නාමය wishesha naamaya proper noun व्यक्तिवाचक संज्ञा 4 සමූහ නාමය samooha naamaya collective noun समूहवाचक संज्ञा 5 ද්රව්ය නාමය drawya naamaya material noun द्रव्यवाचक संज्ञा 6 භාව නාමය bhaawa naamaya abstract noun भाववाचक संज्ञा 7 සජීවී sajiivi living सजीव 8 අජීවී ajiivi non-living निर्जीव 9 පුද්ගලයා puddgalayaa person व्यक्ति 10 සතා sathaa animal प्राणी / जानवर

5.7 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. a noun names a person, place, animal, thing or idea. 2. five kinds: common, proper, collective, material, abstract. 3. living things take ඉන්නවා; non-living things take තියෙනවා. 4. a / one = -ක් (things) and -ෙක් (people): පොතක්, ළමයෙක්. 5. there is no word for “the”.

(a) ළමයා ගෙදර __ (b) පොත මේසය උඩ __ q5. correct the mistake: ගස අංගනයේ ඉන්නවා. q6. write three living and three non-living nouns. part c: “a / one” and translation q7. add the ending: (a) ගම (b) ළමයා (c) මල (d) ගුරුවරයා. q8. translate into sinhala: (a) a teacher is in the class. (b) there is a book on the table. q9. translate into english: ළමයෙක් ගසක් උඩ ඉන්නවා. q10. write one sentence with a proper noun and translate it into hindi.

(b) පොතක් මේසය උඩ තියෙනවා. 5.3, 5.5 9 a child is on a tree. 5.3 10 e.g. කොළඹ ලොකු නගරයක්. कोलंबो एक बड़ा शहर है। 5.2 tip — coming next lesson 6: gender (ලිංග). you will learn masculine, feminine and neuter nouns, and how sinhala differs from hindi.

lesson 6 lesson 6: gender ලිංග लिंग key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the three genders (ලිංග) 2. why sinhala is easier than hindi here 3. masculine and feminine pairs 4. how to form the feminine

6.1 the three genders (ලිංග) නාම පද ලිංග තුනකට බෙදේ. naama pada linga thunakata bede. nouns are divided into three genders. संज्ञाएँ तीन लिंगों में बाँटी जाती हैं। gender meaning examples hindi පුරුෂ ලිංගය purusha lingaya masculine පුතා, තාත්තා, ගුරුවරයා, රජ पुल्लिंग ස්ත්රී ලිංගය sthrii lingaya feminine දුව, අම්මා, ගුරුවරිය, රැජින स्त्रीलिंग නපුංසක ලිංගය napumsaka lingaya neuter (things) පොත, ගස, මේසය, ගෙදර नपुंसक / निर्जीव key idea — good news in hindi every noun is masculine or feminine (किताब is feminine, पेड़ is masculine), and the verb changes with it. in sinhala only people and animals have gender. things are neuter, and the verb never changes for gender in speech.

6.2 hindi and sinhala compared english hindi (verb changes) sinhala (verb same) he goes. / she goes. वह जाता है। / वह जाती है। ඔහු යනවා. / ඇය යනවා. ohu yanawaa / aeya yanawaa he reads. / she reads. वह पढ़ता है। / वह पढ़ती है। ඔහු කියවනවා. / ඇය කියවනවා. ohu kiyawanawaa / aeya kiyawanawaa the teacher (m / f) is here. शिक्षक / शिक्षिका यहाँ है। ගුරුවරයා / ගුරුවරිය මෙහේ ඉන්නවා. guruwarayaa / guruwariya mehe innawaa remember — only the noun changes in sinhala the noun (and the pronoun ඔහු / ඇය) shows gender. the verb does not. in the written style, the past tense verb does show it: ඔහු ගියේය / ඇය ගියාය (lesson 18).

(gentleman / lady) श्रीमान / श्रीमती

6.4 making the feminine masculine ending feminine ending example -යා -ිය ගුරුවරයා → ගුරුවරිය guruwarayaa → guruwariya -කයා -ිකාව ගායකයා → ගායිකාව gaayakayaa → gaayikaawa -යා -ාව ශිෂ්යයා → ශිෂ්යාව shishyayaa → shishyaawa different word different word පුතා / දුව; අයියා / අක්කා puthaa / duwa; ayyaa / akkaa to show the sex of a person or animal without a special word, use පිරිමි (male) and ගැහැණු (female): පිරිමි ළමයා (boy), ගැහැණු ළමයා (girl).

6.5 sentences # sinhala english hindi 1 ගුරුවරයා පාඩම උගන්වනවා. guruwarayaa paadama uganwanawaa the (male) teacher teaches the lesson. शिक्षक पाठ पढ़ाते हैं। 2 ගුරුවරිය පාඩම උගන්වනවා. guruwariya paadama uganwanawaa the (female) teacher teaches the lesson. शिक्षिका पाठ पढ़ाती हैं। 3 ශිෂ්යාව පොත කියවනවා. shishyaawa potha kiyawanawaa the (female) student reads a book. छात्रा किताब पढ़ती है। 4 ගායිකාව ගීතයක් ගායනා කරනවා. gaayikaawa giithayak gaayanaa karanawaa the (female) singer sings a song. गायिका गाना गाती है। 5 වෛද්යවරයා රෝගියාට බෙහෙත් දෙනවා. waidyawarayaa rogiyaata behet denawaa the doctor gives medicine to the patient. डॉक्टर मरीज़ को दवा देते हैं। 6 රජ මාළිගාවේ ඉන්නවා. raja maaligaawe innawaa the king is in the palace. राजा महल में है। 7 ඇතා ගඟට යනවා. aethaa gangata yanawaa the elephant goes to the river. हाथी नदी पर जाता है। 8 කිකිළිය බිත්තර දානවා. kikiliya biththara daanawaa the hen lays eggs. मुर्गी अंडे देती है। 9 නංගි කිරි බොනවා. nangi kiri bonawaa the younger sister drinks milk. छोटी बहन दूध पीती है। 10 අක්කා බත් උයනවා. akkaa bath uyanawaa the older sister cooks rice. दीदी चावल पकाती है।

6.7 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. nouns have three genders: masculine, feminine, neuter. 2. only people and animals have gender; things are neuter. 3. in speech the sinhala verb does not change for gender, unlike hindi. 4. feminine: -යා → -ිය, -කයා → -ිකාව, or a new word. 5. use පිරිමි / ගැහැණු to show the sex.

lesson 7 lesson 7: singular and plural ඒකවචන සහ බහුවචන एकवचन और बहुवचन key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. singular (ඒකවචන) and plural (බහුවචන) 2. plurals of non-living nouns 3. plurals of living nouns and the second plural form 4. counting nouns: one book, two books

7.1 singular and plural එක් අයෙකු හෝ එක් දෙයක් ඒකවචනයයි. එකකට වැඩි ගණන බහුවචනයයි. ek ayeku ho ek deyak ekawachanayayi. ekakata waedi gana bahuwachanayayi. one person or thing is singular. more than one is plural. एक व्यक्ति या वस्तु एकवचन है। एक से अधिक बहुवचन है। sinhala makes plurals by changing the end of the noun. the way depends on whether the noun is non-living (lesson 5) or living. hindi works in a similar way (लड़का → लड़के).

7.2 plurals of non-living nouns rule — rule final -අ: add the sign ් (hal): පොත → පොත්. final -ය or -ව: drop it: මේසය → මේස, පුටුව → පුටු. # singular plural english hindi 1 පොත potha පොත් poth book(s) किताब / किताबें 2 ගස gasa ගස් gas tree(s) पेड़ 3 මල mala මල් mal flower(s) फूल 4 ගම gama ගම් gam village(s) गाँव 5 පෑන paena පෑන් paen pen(s) कलम 6 මේසය mesaya මේස mesa table(s) मेज़ 7 පුටුව putuwa පුටු putu chair(s) कुर्सी 8 කාමරය kaamaraya කාමර kaamara room(s) कमरा 9 ගෙදර gedara ගෙවල් gewal house(s) घर 10 කඩය kadaya කඩ kada shop(s) दुकान 11 ජනේලය janelaya ජනේල janela window(s) खिड़की

7.3 plurals of living nouns (two forms) a living noun has two plural forms. the first is used as the subject. the second is the “base” for case endings (part iii): ළමයින් + ට = ළමයින්ට. # singular 1st plural (subject) 2nd plural (base) english 1 ළමයා lamayaa ළමයෝ lamayo ළමයින් lamayin children 2 ගුරුවරයා guruwarayaa ගුරුවරු guruwaru ගුරුවරුන් guruwarun teachers 3 ශිෂ්යයා shishyayaa ශිෂ්යයෝ shishyayo ශිෂ්යයන් shishyayan students 4 මිනිසා minisaa මිනිස්සු minissu මිනිසුන් minisun men, people 5 ඇතා aethaa ඇත්තු aeththu ඇතුන් aethun elephants 6 කුරුල්ලා kurullaa කුරුල්ලෝ kurullo කුරුල්ලන් kurullan birds 7 බල්ලා ballaa බල්ලෝ ballo බල්ලන් ballan dogs 8 ගොවියා goviyaa ගොවියෝ goviyo ගොවීන් goviin farmers 9 සොල්දාදුවා soldaaduwaa සොල්දාදුවෝ soldaaduwo සොල්දාදුවන් soldaaduwan soldiers 10 දරුවා daruwaa දරුවෝ daruwo දරුවන් daruwan children, sons 11 යාළුවා yaaluwaa යාළුවෝ yaaluwo යාළුවන් yaaluwan friends 12 සතා sathaa සත්තු saththu සතුන් sathun animals tip — family words add -ලා to family words and names: අම්මා → අම්මලා (mothers), තාත්තා → තාත්තලා (fathers), අයියා → අයියලා, අක්කා → අක්කලා, මල්ලි → මල්ලිලා, යාළුවා → යාළුවලා.

7.4 counting: one, two, three … number sinhala things (පොත) people (ළමයා) 1 එක eka පොතක් pothak ළමයෙක් lamayek 2 දෙක deka පොත් දෙකක් poth dekak ළමයි දෙදෙනෙක් lamayi dedenek 3 තුන thuna පොත් තුනක් poth thunak ළමයි තුන්දෙනෙක් lamayi thundenek 4 හතර hathara පොත් හතරක් poth hatharak ළමයි හතරදෙනෙක් lamayi hatharadenek 5 පහ paha පොත් පහක් poth pahak ළමයි පස්දෙනෙක් lamayi pasdenek rule — rule after a number, the noun is plural and -ක් is added to the number for things: පොත් දෙකක්. for people, the number takes -දෙනෙක්: දෙදෙනෙක්, තුන්දෙනෙක්.

7.5 sentences # sinhala english hindi 1 ළමයෝ පාසලට යනවා. lamayo paasalata yanawaa the children go to school. बच्चे स्कूल जाते हैं। 2 ගුරුවරු පාඩම් උගන්වනවා. guruwaru paadam uganwanawaa the teachers teach lessons. शिक्षक पाठ पढ़ाते हैं। 3 මල් පිපෙනවා. mal pipenawaa flowers bloom. फूल खिलते हैं। 4 මේසය උඩ පොත් දෙකක් තියෙනවා. mesaya uda poth dekak thiyenawaa there are two books on the table. मेज़ पर दो किताबें हैं। 5 කුරුල්ලෝ ගසේ ඉන්නවා. kurullo gase innawaa the birds are in the tree. चिड़ियाँ पेड़ पर हैं। 6 සොල්දාදුවෝ කඳවුරට යනවා. soldaaduwo kandawurata yanawaa the soldiers go to the camp. सैनिक शिविर जाते हैं। 7 ගොවියෝ කුඹුරේ වැඩ කරනවා. goviyo kumbure wae kaaranawaa the farmers work in the field. किसान खेत में काम करते हैं। 8 අපේ ගෙවල් ලොකුයි. ape gewal lokuyi our houses are big. हमारे घर बड़े हैं। 9 යාළුවෝ තුන්දෙනෙක් ආවා. yaaluwo thundenek aawaa three friends came. तीन दोस्त आए। 10 ගස් පහක් මෙතන තියෙනවා. gas pahak methana thiyenawaa there are five trees here. यहाँ पाँच पेड़ हैं।

7.6 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 ඒකවචනය ekawachanaya singular एकवचन 2 බහුවචනය bahuwachanaya plural बहुवचन 3 ගණන gana number, count संख्या 4 එක eka one एक 5 දෙක deka two दो 6 තුන thuna three तीन 7 හතර hathara four चार 8 පහ paha five पाँच 9 කුඹුර kumbura paddy field खेत 10 කඳවුර kandawura camp शिविर

7.7 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. non-living plural: final -අ takes ් (පොත්); final -ය / -ව drops (මේස, පුටු). 2. living nouns have two plurals: subject form (ළමයෝ) and base form (ළමයින්). 3. family words take -ලා: අම්මලා. 4. numbers: පොත් දෙකක්, ළමයි දෙදෙනෙක්.

7.8 practice questions (අභ්යාස) part a: non-living plurals q1. make the plural: පොත, ගස, මේසය, පුටුව, ගෙදර. q2. write the singular: මල්, ගම්, කාමර, ජනේල. part b: living plurals q3. write both plural forms: ළමයා, ගුරුවරයා, කුරුල්ලා. q4. make the plural with -ලා: අම්මා, අක්කා, යාළුවා. q5. what is the plural of මිනිසා and ඇතා? part c: counting and sentences q6. write in sinhala: two books, three flowers, five trees. q7. write in sinhala: one child, two children, three friends. q8. translate into sinhala: the children go to school. q9. translate into english: මේසය උඩ පොත් දෙකක් තියෙනවා. q10. write in sinhala: four books, five children.

7.9 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 පොත්, ගස්, මේස, පුටු, ගෙවල් 7.2 2 මල, ගම, කාමරය, ජනේලය 7.2 3 ළමයෝ / ළමයින්; ගුරුවරු / ගුරුවරුන්; කුරුල්ලෝ / කුරුල්ලන් 7.3 4 අම්මලා, අක්කලා, යාළුවලා 7.3 5 මිනිස්සු / මිනිසුන්; ඇත්තු / ඇතුන් 7.3 6 පොත් දෙකක්, මල් තුනක්, ගස් පහක් 7.4 7 ළමයෙක්, ළමයි දෙදෙනෙක්, යාළුවෝ තුන්දෙනෙක් 7.4 8 ළමයෝ පාසලට යනවා. 7.5 9 there are two books on the table. 7.5 10 පොත් හතරක්; ළමයි පස්දෙනෙක් 7.4 tip — coming next lesson 8: pronouns (සර්වනාම). you will learn the personal, demonstrative and question pronouns, and their forms.

lesson 8 lesson 8: pronouns සර්වනාම सर्वनाम key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what a pronoun (සර්වනාමය) is 2. the personal pronouns: i, we, you, he, she, it, they 3. levels of respect 4. this / that, and question words 5. pronoun forms: me, my, to me

8.1 what is a pronoun? නාමයක් වෙනුවට යෙදෙන පදය සර්වනාමයයි. naamayak wenuwata yedena padaya sarwanaamayayi. a word used in place of a noun is a pronoun. संज्ञा के स्थान पर प्रयुक्त शब्द सर्वनाम कहलाता है। instead of repeating “nimal”, we say “he”. in sinhala, pronouns are divided into three persons: the speaker (1st), the person spoken to (2nd), and the person spoken about (3rd). pronouns are the first words every learner must memorise.

8.2 the personal pronouns person spoken written hindi english 1st sing. මම / මං mama / mang මම mama मैं i 1st plural අපි api අපි api हम we 2nd sing. ඔයා oyaa ඔබ oba तुम / आप you 2nd plural ඔයාලා oyaalaa ඔබලා obalaa तुम लोग / आप लोग you (all) 3rd masc. ඔහු / එයා ohu / eyaa ඔහු ohu वह (पु.) he 3rd fem. ඇය / එයා aeya / eyaa ඇය aeya वह (स्त्री.) she 3rd neuter ඒක eeka එය eya वह / यह it 3rd plural ඔවුන් / උන් owun / un ඔවුන් / ඔවුහු owun / owuhu वे they key idea — remember ඔහු is used for males, ඇය for females and එය for things. ඔවුන් (they) is used for people of both sexes.

8.3 levels of respect like hindi (तू – तुम – आप), sinhala has several words for “you”. using the wrong one can be rude. sinhala hindi when to use ඔබතුමා / ඔබතුමිය obathumaa / obathumiya आप (अत्यंत आदर) a teacher, officer or elder; also in speeches and letters ඔබ oba आप polite; written sinhala, notices, and addressing strangers ඔයා oyaa तुम friends, family of the same age, everyday talk තෝ thoo तू very close friends only, or rude. do not use as a learner. remember — safe rule for learners use ඔබ to a stranger or senior, and ඔබතුමා / ඔබතුමිය to a very senior person. use ඔයා only with friends.

8.4 this, that and question words meaning spoken written hindi this (thing) මේක meeka මෙය meya यह that (thing) ඒක eeka එය eya वह that over there අරක araka අරය araya वह (दूर) this … (before a noun) මේ mee මෙම mema यह … that … (before a noun) ඒ ee එම ema वह … question words (ප්රශ්නාර්ථ සර්වනාම): # english spoken written hindi 1 who? කවුද? kawuda කවුරුන්ද? kawurunda कौन 2 what? මොකක්ද? mokakda කුමක්ද? kumakda क्या 3 where? කොහෙද? kohedha කොහිද? kohida कहाँ 4 when? කවදාද? kawadaada කවදාද? kawadaada कब 5 why? ඇයි? aeyi මන්ද? manda क्यों 6 how? කොහොමද? kohomada කෙසේද? kesedha कैसे 7 which? මොන? mona කුමන? kumana कौन सा

lesson 9 lesson 9: adjectives විශේෂණ विशेषण key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what an adjective (විශේෂණය) is 2. kinds of adjectives and their position 3. the ending -යි (“is …”) 4. comparing: taller, tallest

9.1 what is an adjective? නාමයක ගුණය හෝ ස්වභාවය දක්වන පදය විශේෂණයයි. naamayaka gunaya ho swabhaawaya dakwana padaya wisheshanayayi. a word that tells the quality of a noun is an adjective. संज्ञा की विशेषता बताने वाला शब्द विशेषण कहलाता है। key idea — two good rules 1. the adjective comes before the noun: ලස්සන මල (beautiful flower), as in hindi: सुंदर फूल. 2. the adjective never changes for gender or number. hindi: अच्छा लड़का, अच्छी लड़की. sinhala: හොඳ ළමයා, හොඳ ළමිය, හොඳ ළමයි.

9.2 common adjectives # sinhala opposite english hindi 1 ලොකු loku පොඩි podi big / small बड़ा / छोटा 2 උස usa මිටි miti tall / short ऊँचा / नाटा 3 හොඳ honda නරක naraka good / bad अच्छा / बुरा 4 අළුත් alut පරණ parana new / old नया / पुराना 5 ලස්සන lassana කැතයි kaethayi beautiful / ugly सुंदर / बदसूरत 6 උණුසුම් unusum සීතල siithala hot / cold गरम / ठंडा 7 දිගු digu කෙටි keti long / short लंबा / छोटा 8 සැහැල්ලු saehaellu බර bara light / heavy हल्का / भारी 9 රසවත් rasawath තිත්ත thiththa tasty / bitter स्वादिष्ट / कड़वा 10 සුදු sudu කළු kalu white / black सफ़ेद / काला colours: රතු (red), නිල් (blue), කොළ (green), කහ (yellow), රෝස (pink), දුඹුරු (brown), සුදු (white), කළු (black).

9.3 other kinds of adjectives kind examples sentence number එක, දෙක, තුන, හතර පොත් තුනක් – three books poth thunak quantity බොහෝ (many), සියලු (all), ටිකක් (a few) බොහෝ ළමයි – many children bohoo lamayi pointing මේ (this), ඒ (that), අර (that over there) මේ පොත – this book mee potha question මොන / කුමන (which?) මොන පොත? – which book? mona potha
9.4  Adjective in the Predicate: the Ending -යි

9.4 adjective in the predicate: the ending -යි when the adjective comes after the noun and says “is …”, we add -යි to it (spoken): # sinhala english hindi 1 මේ මල ලස්සනයි. mee mala lassanayi this flower is beautiful. यह फूल सुंदर है। 2 ගස උසයි. gasa usayi the tree is tall. पेड़ ऊँचा है। 3 ගෙදර ලොකුයි. gedara lokuyi the house is big. घर बड़ा है। 4 වතුර සීතලයි. watura siithalayi the water is cold. पानी ठंडा है। 5 පොත අළුත්. potha alut the book is new. किताब नई है। tip — written style written sinhala usually adds -ය or -යි: මෙම මල ලස්සනය / ලස්සනයි.

9.5 comparing: -er and -est degree rule example comparative (more) “than” + ට + වඩා ඔහු ඇයට වඩා උසයි. ohu aeyata wadaa usayi – he is taller than her. superlative (most) ඉතාම or සියල්ලටම වඩා මේ ගස ඉතාම උසයි. mee gasa ithaama usayi – this tree is the tallest. very ඉතා / ගොඩක් මේ කෑම ඉතා රසයි. mee kaaema ithaa rasayi – this food is very tasty. # sinhala english hindi 1 අයියා මට වඩා උසයි. ayyaa mata wadaa usayi my elder brother is taller than me. भैया मुझसे लंबे हैं। 2 මේ පොත ඒකට වඩා ලොකුයි. mee potha eekata wadaa lokuyi this book is bigger than that one. यह किताब उससे बड़ी है। 3 ඇය පන්තියේ ඉතාම දක්ෂයි. aeya panthiye ithaama dakshayi she is the cleverest in the class. वह कक्षा में सबसे होशियार है।

9.6 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 විශේෂණය wisheshanaya adjective विशेषण 2 ගුණය gunaya quality गुण 3 ලොකු loku big बड़ा 4 පොඩි podi small छोटा 5 ලස්සන lassana beautiful सुंदर 6 උස usa tall ऊँचा 7 දක්ෂ daksha clever, skilled होशियार 8 වඩා wadaa more than से अधिक 9 ඉතාම ithaama most, very सबसे / बहुत 10 සියලු siyalu all सभी

9.7 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. the adjective comes before the noun. 2. it does not change for gender or number. 3. after the noun, add -යි: මල ලස්සනයි. 4. compare with ට … වඩා; superlative with ඉතාම.

Lesson 10: What Is a Case? The Eight Cases at a Glance

lesson 10 lesson 10: what is a case? the eight cases at a glance විභක්ති හැඳින්වීම विभक्ति (कारक) का परिचय key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what a case (විභක්තිය) is, and why sinhala needs it 2. the eight cases, with their hindi names 3. the question that finds each case 4. how to find the case of a word in a sentence

10.1 what is a case? (විභක්තිය) වාක්යයක නාමයක් අනෙක් පද සමඟ ඇති සම්බන්ධය විභක්තියෙන් දැක්වේ. waakyayaka naamayak aneka pada samaga aethi sambandhaya wibhakthiyen daekwe. a case shows how a noun is related to the other words in the sentence. विभक्ति वाक्य में संज्ञा का अन्य शब्दों से संबंध दिखाती है। english shows these relations with little words (to, from, of, in) and with word order. hindi uses little words after the noun (को, से, का, में). sinhala puts an ending on the noun (or a little word after it). this is why the case endings are the heart of sinhala grammar. compare: meaning english hindi sinhala to the child to the child बच्चे को ළමයාට lamayaata of the child the child’s बच्चे का ළමයාගේ lamayaage from the village from the village गाँव से ගමෙන් gamen in the village in the village गाँव में ගමේ game key idea — good news sinhala has the same eight cases as sanskrit and hindi grammar. even the hindi names (कर्ता, कर्म, करण, सम्प्रदान, अपादान, सम्बन्ध, अधिकरण, सम्बोधन) are the same ideas, so you already know the plan.

10.2 the eight cases # sinhala english hindi job of the case question 1 ප්රථමා prathamaa nominative कर्ता the doer (subject) කවුද? who? 2 ද්විතීයා dwithiiyaa accusative कर्म the one acted upon (object) කාවද? මොකක්ද? whom? what? 3 තෘතීයා thruthiiyaa instrumental करण with, by (tool, means, doer in passive) කුමකින්ද? with what? 4 චතුර්ථී chathurthii dative सम्प्रदान to, for (receiver, goal) කාටද? to whom? 5 පඤ්චමී panchamii ablative अपादान from (source, separation) කොහෙන්ද? කාගෙන්ද? from where / whom? 6 ෂෂ්ඨී shashtii genitive सम्बन्ध of (owner, relation) කාගේද? whose? 7 සප්තමී sapthamii locative अधिकरण in, on, at (place, time) කොහෙද? where? 8 ආලපන aalapana vocative सम्बोधन calling a person — o …! another name for the 1st case is කර්තෘ (doer), for the 2nd කර්ම, for the 3rd කරණ, for the 4th සම්ප්රදාන, for the 5th අපාදාන, for the 6th සම්බන්ධ and for the 7th ආධාර. you will see both names in books. learn them in pairs.

10.3 one noun in eight cases look at how a living noun (ළමයා, child) and a non-living noun (ගම, village) change. the full tables are in lesson 15. # case ළමයා (living) ගම (non-living) meaning 1 nominative ළමයා lamayaa ගම gama the child / the village 2 accusative ළමයාව lamayaawa ගම gama (sees) the child / village 3 instrumental ළමයා විසින් lamayaa wisin ගමෙන් gamen by the child / by the village 4 dative ළමයාට lamayaata ගමට gamata to the child / village 5 ablative ළමයාගෙන් lamayaagen ගමෙන් gamen from the child / village 6 genitive ළමයාගේ lamayaage ගමේ game of the child / village 7 locative ළමයා ළඟ lamayaa langa ගමේ game near the child / in the village 8 vocative ළමයෝ! lamayo — o child!
10.4  How to Find the Case of a Word

10.4 how to find the case of a word find the verb → ask who / what does it? → ask whom / where / with what / from where / whose → name the case from the question analyse these sentences: # sentence cases 1 ළමයා ගමෙන් ආවා. lamayaa gamen aawaa – the child came from the village. ළමයා = nominative; ගමෙන් = ablative (from where?) 2 අම්මා ළමයාට කිරි දුන්නා. ammaa lamayaata kiri dunnaa – mother gave milk to the child. අම්මා = nominative; ළමයාට = dative (to whom?); කිරි = accusative (what?) 3 ගුරුවරයාගේ පොත මේසය උඩ තියෙනවා. guruwarayaage potha mesaya uda thiyenawaa – the teacher’s book is on the table. ගුරුවරයාගේ = genitive (whose?); පොත = nominative; මේසය උඩ = locative (where?) 4 මම පෑනෙන් ලිපියක් ලියනවා. mama paenen lipiyak liyanawaa – i write a letter with a pen. මම = nominative; පෑනෙන් = instrumental (with what?); ලිපියක් = accusative 5 අම්මේ, මෙහෙ එන්න! ammee, mehe enna – mother, come here! අම්මේ = vocative (calling)

10.6 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. a case shows the relation of a noun to the other words. 2. sinhala has eight cases: nominative, accusative, instrumental, dative, ablative, genitive, locative, vocative. 3. each case has two names: ප්රථමා / කර්තෘ, ද්විතීයා / කර්ම, තෘතීයා / කරණ, චතුර්ථී / සම්ප්රදාන, පඤ්චමී / අපාදාන, ෂෂ්ඨී / සම්බන්ධ, සප්තමී / ආධාර, ආලපන. 4. to find a case, find the verb and ask who / whom / where / from where / whose.

10.7 practice questions (අභ්යාස) part a: names and meanings q1. write the eight cases in sinhala and english. q2. write the hindi name of each case. q3. which case answers the question කාගේද? q4. which case answers the question කොහෙන්ද? part b: finding the case q5. name the case of the word in bold: ළමයා ගමට යනවා. q6. name the case: ගුරුවරයාගේ පොත. q7. name the case: මම පෑනෙන් ලියනවා. q8. name the case: අක්කේ, මෙහෙ එන්න. part c: translation q9. translate into sinhala: from the village; to the village; of the village; in the village. q10. translate into english: අම්මා ළමයාට කිරි දුන්නා.

lesson 11 lesson 11: nominative and accusative cases ප්රථමා සහ ද්විතීයා විභක්ති कर्ता और कर्म कारक key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the nominative case (ප්රථමා): the doer 2. the accusative case (ද්විතීයා): the object 3. when the ending -ව is needed, and when it is not 4. pronoun forms: මාව, ඔහුව, ඇයව

11.1 the nominative case (ප්රථමා) – the doer ක්රියාව කරන්නා කර්තෘ ය. එය ප්රථමා විභක්තියෙන් දැක්වේ. kriyaawa karannaa karthru ya. eya prathamaa wibhakthiyen daekwe. the one who does the action is the doer (subject). it is shown in the nominative case. क्रिया करने वाला कर्ता है। वह कर्ता कारक में होता है। rule — rule the nominative is the basic form of the noun, with no ending: ළමයා, අම්මා, පොත, ගම. question: කවුද? (who?) or මොකක්ද? (what?) does the action. plural: ළමයෝ, ගුරුවරු, පොත්. # sinhala english hindi 1 ළමයා පාසලට යනවා. lamayaa paasalata yanawaa the child goes to school. बच्चा स्कूल जाता है। 2 අම්මා කෑම උයනවා. ammaa kaaema uyanawaa mother cooks food. माँ खाना पकाती है। 3 ගුරුවරයා පාඩම උගන්වනවා. guruwarayaa paadama uganwanawaa the teacher teaches the lesson. शिक्षक पाठ पढ़ाते हैं। 4 කුරුල්ලා පියාසර කරනවා. kurullaa piyaasara karanawaa the bird flies. चिड़िया उड़ती है। 5 ගස වැටුණා. gasa waetunaa the tree fell. पेड़ गिर गया। 6 සූර්යයා උදාවෙනවා. suuryayaa udaawenawaa the sun rises. सूरज उगता है। 7 වැස්ස වහිනවා. waessa wahinawaa the rain is falling. बारिश हो रही है। 8 බල්ලා බුරනවා. ballaa buranawaa the dog barks. कुत्ता भौंकता है। 9 අපි ගමට යනවා. api gamata yanawaa we go to the village. हम गाँव जाते हैं। 10 ඔහු පත්තරය කියවනවා. ohu paththaraya kiyawanawaa he reads the newspaper. वह अख़बार पढ़ता है। 11 ශිෂ්යයෝ පන්තියේ ඉන්නවා. shishyayo panthiye innawaa the students are in the class. विद्यार्थी कक्षा में हैं। 12 මල්ලි නිදාගන්නවා. malli nidaagannawaa the younger brother sleeps. छोटा भाई सोता है।

11.2 the accusative case (ද්විතීයා) – the object ක්රියාවෙන් බලපෑමට ලක්වන්නා කර්මය ය. kriyaawen balapaemata lakwannaa karmaya ya. the one who receives the action is the object. क्रिया का फल पाने वाला कर्म है। rule — rule living objects (people, animals): add -ව: ළමයා → ළමයාව, ඔහු → ඔහුව. non-living objects (things): no change: පොත කියවනවා, බත් කනවා. question: කාවද? (whom?) for living, මොකක්ද? (what?) for things. key idea — same as hindi hindi also marks the living object with को (मैंने बच्चे को देखा) and leaves the thing unmarked (मैंने किताब पढ़ी). sinhala follows the same idea with -ව. # nominative accusative english hindi 1 ළමයා lamayaa ළමයාව lamayaawa the child बच्चे को 2 ගුරුවරයා guruwarayaa ගුරුවරයාව guruwarayaawa the teacher शिक्षक को 3 අම්මා ammaa අම්මාව ammaawa the mother माँ को 4 මල්ලි malli මල්ලිව malliwa the younger brother छोटे भाई को 5 බල්ලා ballaa බල්ලාව ballaawa the dog कुत्ते को 6 ළමයෝ lamayo ළමයින්ව lamayinwa the children बच्चों को 7 මම mama මාව maawa me मुझे 8 ඔහු ohu ඔහුව ohuwa him उसे 9 ඇය aeya ඇයව aeyawa her उसे 10 ඔබ oba ඔබව obawa you आपको

11.3 accusative sentences # sinhala english hindi 1 මම ළමයාව දැක්කා. mama lamayaawa daekkaa i saw the child. मैंने बच्चे को देखा। 2 ගුරුවරයා ශිෂ්යයාව කැඳවනවා. guruwarayaa shishyayaawa kaedawanawaa the teacher calls the student. शिक्षक विद्यार्थी को बुलाते हैं। 3 අම්මා දරුවාව නාවනවා. ammaa daruwaawa naawanawaa mother bathes the child. माँ बच्चे को नहलाती है। 4 මම මල්ලිව සොයනවා. mama malliwa soyanawaa i am looking for my younger brother. मैं छोटे भाई को ढूँढ़ रहा हूँ। 5 ඔහු බල්ලාව බලනවා. ohu ballaawa balanawaa he looks at the dog. वह कुत्ते को देखता है। 6 අපි ඔහුව හඳුනනවා. api ohuwa handunanawaa we know (recognise) him. हम उसे पहचानते हैं। 7 ඇය ළමයාව බේරුවා. aeya lamayaawa beruwaa she saved the child. उसने बच्चे को बचाया। 8 මම පොත කියවනවා. mama potha kiyawanawaa i read the book. (thing: no change) मैं किताब पढ़ता हूँ। 9 අම්මා බත් උයනවා. ammaa bath uyanawaa mother cooks rice. माँ चावल पकाती है। 10 මම වතුර බොනවා. mama watura bonawaa i drink water. मैं पानी पीता हूँ। 11 ඔහු ලිපියක් ලියනවා. ohu lipiyak liyanawaa he writes a letter. वह पत्र लिखता है। 12 අපි ගෙයක් හදනවා. api geyak hadanawaa we build a house. हम घर बनाते हैं। remember — common mistake do not add -ව to things: “පොතව කියවනවා” is wrong. say පොත කියවනවා. do not forget it for people: “ළමයා දැක්කා” is wrong when ළමයා is the object. say ළමයාව දැක්කා.

11.4 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 ප්රථමා prathamaa nominative कर्ता कारक 2 ද්විතීයා dwithiiyaa accusative कर्म कारक 3 කර්තෘ karthru doer कर्ता 4 කර්මය karmaya object कर्म 5 දකිනවා dakinawaa sees देखता है 6 බලනවා balanawaa looks at, watches देखता है / ताकता है 7 සොයනවා soyanawaa searches for ढूँढ़ता है 8 හඳුනනවා handunanawaa recognises, knows (a person) पहचानता है 9 බේරනවා beranawaa saves, rescues बचाता है 10 කැඳවනවා kaedawanawaa calls, summons बुलाता है

11.5 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. nominative: the doer, no ending (ළමයා), asks කවුද? 2. accusative: the object. living: add -ව (ළමයාව). things: no change (පොත). 3. pronouns: මාව, ඔබව, ඔහුව, ඇයව, අපව, ඔවුන්ව. 4. hindi parallel: living object + को.

11.6 practice questions (අභ්යාස) part a: nominative q1. what question finds the nominative? q2. pick the nominative: ගුරුවරයා පාඩම උගන්වනවා. q3. pick the nominative: ගස වැටුණා. part b: accusative q4. add the ending where needed: (a) මම ළමයා දැක්කා (b) මම පොත කියවනවා (c) ඔහු මල්ලි සොයනවා. q5. write the accusative of: අම්මා, බල්ලා, ඔහු, ඇය, මම. q6. why do we say ළමයාව දැක්කා but පොත කියවනවා? part c: sentences q7. translate into sinhala: mother bathes the child. q8. translate into sinhala: we know him. q9. translate into english: ඇය ළමයාව බේරුවා. q10. translate into english: ගුරුවරයා ශිෂ්යයාව කැඳවනවා.

11.7 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 කවුද? (who?) or මොකක්ද? (what?) 11.1 2 ගුරුවරයා 11.1 3 ගස 11.1 4 (a) ළමයාව (b) පොත (no change) (c) මල්ලිව 11.2 5 අම්මාව, බල්ලාව, ඔහුව, ඇයව, මාව 11.2 6 living objects take -ව; things do not (like hindi को) 11.2 7 අම්මා දරුවාව නාවනවා. 11.3 8 අපි ඔහුව හඳුනනවා. 11.3 9 she saved the child. 11.3 10 the teacher calls the student. 11.3 tip — coming next lesson 12: instrumental (තෘතීයා) and dative (චතුර්ථී). “with, by” and “to, for”.

lesson 12 lesson 12: instrumental and dative cases තෘතීයා සහ චතුර්ථී විභක්ති करण और सम्प्रदान कारक key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the instrumental case (තෘතීයා): with, by 2. the agent word විසින් and the word සමඟ (with) 3. the dative case (චතුර්ථී): to, for 4. pronouns: මට, අපට, ඔබට, ඔහුට, ඇයට, ඔවුන්ට

12.1 the instrumental case (තෘතීයා) – “with, by” ක්රියාව කිරීමට උපකාරී වන දෙය කරණය ය. kriyaawa kireemata upakaari wana deya karanaya ya. the thing that helps in doing the action is the instrument. क्रिया करने में सहायक वस्तु करण कहलाती है। rule — rule add -ෙන් or -ින් to a non-living noun: පෑන → පෑනෙන්, අත → අතින්, බසය → බසයෙන්. question: කුමකින්ද? / මොකෙන්ද? (with what? by what?). for the doer in a passive sentence (“written by the teacher”), use විසින්: ගුරුවරයා විසින්. “with a person” (company) is not this case. use සමඟ / එක්ක: යාළුවා සමඟ. # sinhala english hindi 1 මම පෑනෙන් ලියනවා. mama paenen liyanawaa i write with a pen. मैं कलम से लिखता हूँ। 2 ඇය පිහියෙන් එළවළු කපනවා. aeya pihiyen elawalu kapanawaa she cuts vegetables with a knife. वह चाकू से सब्ज़ी काटती है। 3 ඔහු අතින් කනවා. ohu athin kanawaa he eats with his hand. वह हाथ से खाता है। 4 අපි බසයෙන් යනවා. api basayen yanawaa we go by bus. हम बस से जाते हैं। 5 මම දුම්රියෙන් යනවා. mama dumriyen yanawaa i go by train. मैं रेल से जाता हूँ। 6 ළමයා ඇසින් දකිනවා. lamayaa aesin dakinawaa the child sees with the eyes. बच्चा आँखों से देखता है। 7 මම වතුරෙන් අත් සෝදනවා. mama waturen ath sodanawaa i wash my hands with water. मैं पानी से हाथ धोता हूँ। 8 අපි පැන්සලෙන් චිත්ර අඳිනවා. api paensalen chithra andinawaa we draw pictures with a pencil. हम पेंसिल से चित्र बनाते हैं। 9 ඔහු සතුටින් ආවා. ohu sathutin aawaa he came happily. वह खुशी से आया। 10 අධ්යාපනයෙන් රට දියුණු වෙනවා. adhyaapanayen rata diyunu wenawaa a country progresses through education. शिक्षा से देश उन्नति करता है। 11 මේ ලිපිය ගුරුවරයා විසින් ලියන ලදී. mee lipiya guruwarayaa wisin liyana ladii this letter was written by the teacher. यह पत्र शिक्षक द्वारा लिखा गया। 12 මම යාළුවා සමඟ යනවා. mama yaaluwaa samaga yanawaa i go with my friend. मैं दोस्त के साथ जाता हूँ।

12.2 the dative case (චතුර්ථී) – “to, for” දීම, යාම ආදියෙන් යමක් ලබන්නා සම්ප්රදානය ය. deema, yaama aadiyen yamak labannaa sampradaanaya ya. the one who receives (by giving, going, etc.) is the recipient. देने, जाने आदि से जो कुछ पाता है वह सम्प्रदान है। rule — rule add -ට to the noun: ළමයා → ළමයාට, ගම → ගමට, පාසල → පාසලට. question: කාටද? (to whom?) or කොහෙටද? (to where?). it also means “for the sake of”: ළමයා සඳහා / වෙනුවෙන්. many feelings and needs take it: මට බඩගිනියි (i am hungry), මට පොතක් ඕනෑ (i need a book). # pronoun dative english hindi 1 මම mama මට mata to me मुझे 2 අපි api අපට apata to us हमें 3 ඔබ oba ඔබට obata to you आपको 4 ඔහු ohu ඔහුට ohuta to him उसे 5 ඇය aeya ඇයට aeyata to her उसे 6 ඔවුන් owun ඔවුන්ට owunta to them उन्हें # sinhala english hindi 1 මම ගුරුවරයාට පොත දුන්නා. mama guruwarayaata potha dunnaa i gave the book to the teacher. मैंने शिक्षक को किताब दी। 2 අම්මා දරුවාට කිරි දෙනවා. ammaa daruwaata kiri denawaa mother gives milk to the child. माँ बच्चे को दूध देती है। 3 ඔහු මට කතා කළා. ohu mata kathaa kalaa he spoke to me. उसने मुझसे बात की। 4 අපි ගමට යනවා. api gamata yanawaa we go to the village. हम गाँव जाते हैं। 5 ළමයා පාසලට යනවා. lamayaa paasalata yanawaa the child goes to school. बच्चा स्कूल जाता है। 6 මට බඩගිනියි. mata badaginiyi i am hungry. मुझे भूख लगी है। 7 මට පොතක් ඕනෑ. mata pothak oonae i need a book. मुझे एक किताब चाहिए। 8 ඇයට සිංහල තේරෙනවා. aeyata sinhala therenawaa she understands sinhala. उसे सिंहली समझ आती है। 9 ඔහු ඇයට ලිපියක් ලිව්වා. ohu aeyata lipiyak liwwaa he wrote a letter to her. उसने उसे पत्र लिखा। 10 වෛද්යවරයා රෝගියාට බෙහෙත් දෙනවා. waidyawarayaa rogiyaata behet denawaa the doctor gives medicine to the patient. डॉक्टर मरीज़ को दवा देते हैं। 11 මේ පොත ළමයාට. mee potha lamayaata this book is for the child. यह किताब बच्चे के लिए है।

12.3 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 තෘතීයා thruthiiyaa instrumental case करण कारक 2 චතුර්ථී chathurthii dative case सम्प्रदान कारक 3 විසින් wisin by (the doer) द्वारा 4 සමඟ / එක්ක samaga / ekka with (company) के साथ 5 සඳහා / වෙනුවෙන් sandahaa / wenuwen for, for the sake of के लिए 6 පිහිය pihiya knife चाकू 7 පැන්සල paensala pencil पेंसिल 8 බඩගිනි badagini hunger, hungry भूख 9 බෙහෙත behetha medicine दवा 10 තේරෙනවා therenawaa understands (it is clear to) समझ आता है

12.4 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. instrumental: -ෙන් / -ින් (with a tool); විසින් (doer in passive); සමඟ (with a person). 2. dative: -ට (to, for). question: කාටද? 3. pronouns: මට, අපට, ඔබට, ඔහුට, ඇයට, ඔවුන්ට. 4. feelings and needs use the dative: මට බඩගිනියි, මට පොතක් ඕනෑ.

12.5 practice questions (අභ්යාස) part a: instrumental q1. add the ending: (a) පෑන (b) අත (c) පිහිය (d) බසය. q2. which word shows the doer in “written by the teacher”? q3. translate: with my friend. part b: dative q4. add the ending: (a) ගුරුවරයා (b) ගම (c) පාසල (d) රෝගියා. q5. write the dative of: මම, අපි, ඔහු, ඇය. q6. translate: i am hungry. part c: sentences q7. translate into sinhala: i write with a pen. q8. translate into sinhala: mother gives milk to the child. q9. translate into english: අපි බසයෙන් ගමට යනවා. q10. translate into english: ඇය පිහියෙන් එළවළු කපනවා.

12.6 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 (a) පෑනෙන් (b) අතින් (c) පිහියෙන් (d) බසයෙන් 12.1 2 විසින් 12.1 3 යාළුවා සමඟ / යාළුවා එක්ක 12.1 4 (a) ගුරුවරයාට (b) ගමට (c) පාසලට (d) රෝගියාට 12.2 5 මට, අපට, ඔහුට, ඇයට 12.2 6 මට බඩගිනියි. 12.2 7 මම පෑනෙන් ලියනවා. 12.1 8 අම්මා දරුවාට කිරි දෙනවා. 12.2 9 we go to the village by bus. 12.1–12.2 10 she cuts vegetables with a knife. 12.1 tip — coming next lesson 13: ablative (පඤ්චමී) and genitive (ෂෂ්ඨී). “from” and “of”.

lesson 13 lesson 13: ablative and genitive cases පඤ්චමී සහ ෂෂ්ඨී විභක්ති अपादान और सम्बन्ध कारक key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the ablative case (පඤ්චමී): from 2. living and non-living endings: -ගෙන් and -ෙන් 3. the genitive case (ෂෂ්ඨී): of, belonging to 4. pronouns: මගේ, අපේ, ඔබේ, ඔහුගේ, ඇයගේ, ඔවුන්ගේ

13.1 the ablative case (පඤ්චමී) – “from” යමකින් වෙන්වීම අපාදානය ය. yamakin wenweema apaadaanaya ya. separation or starting from something is the ablative. किसी से अलग होना अपादान कहलाता है। rule — rule non-living nouns: add -ෙන් / -ින්: ගම → ගමෙන්, ගෙදර → ගෙදරින්, පාසල → පාසලෙන්. living nouns: add -ගෙන්: ළමයා → ළමයාගෙන්, ගුරුවරයා → ගුරුවරයාගෙන්. question: කොහෙන්ද? (from where?) and කාගෙන්ද? (from whom?). uses: coming from, learning from, asking from, falling from, and also the cause (මරණයෙන්, බයෙන් = out of fear). remember — same look, different job for non-living nouns the instrumental and ablative look alike: ගමෙන්. decide by meaning: “by a tool” = instrumental (පෑනෙන්), “from a place” = ablative (ගමෙන්). # sinhala english hindi 1 ළමයා ගමෙන් ආවා. lamayaa gamen aawaa the child came from the village. बच्चा गाँव से आया। 2 මම ගෙදරින් පිටත් වුණා. mama gedarin pitath wunaa i left from home. मैं घर से निकला। 3 ගසින් කොළ වැටෙනවා. gasin kola waetenawaa leaves fall from the tree. पेड़ से पत्ते गिरते हैं। 4 ඔහු පාසලෙන් ආවා. ohu paasalen aawaa he came from school. वह स्कूल से आया। 5 මම ගුරුවරයාගෙන් ඉගෙන ගත්තා. mama guruwarayaagen igena gaththaa i learned from the teacher. मैंने शिक्षक से सीखा। 6 ළමයා අම්මාගෙන් කිරි ඉල්ලුවා. lamayaa ammaagen kiri illuwaa the child asked mother for milk. बच्चे ने माँ से दूध माँगा। 7 මම යාළුවාගෙන් පොතක් ඉල්ලුවා. mama yaaluwaagen pothak illuwaa i asked a friend for a book. मैंने दोस्त से एक किताब माँगी। 8 ඔහු බයෙන් වෙව්ලනවා. ohu bayen wewlanawaa he trembles with fear. वह डर से काँपता है। 9 ඉරෙන් එළිය එනවා. irein eliya enawaa light comes from the sun. सूरज से रोशनी आती है। 10 ඔහු ශ්රී ලංකාවෙන් ආවා. ohu shrii lankaawen aawaa he came from sri lanka. वह श्रीलंका से आया। 11 මම ඔහුගෙන් ප්රශ්නයක් ඇහුවා. mama ohugen prashnayak aehuwaa i asked him a question. मैंने उससे एक प्रश्न पूछा। 12 මේසයෙන් පොත වැටුණා. mesayen potha waetunaa the book fell from the table. मेज़ से किताब गिर गई।

13.2 the genitive case (ෂෂ්ඨී) – “of” අයිතිය හෝ සම්බන්ධය දැක්වීම ෂෂ්ඨී විභක්තියයි. ayithiya ho sambandhaya daekweema shashtii wibhakthiyayi. showing ownership or relation is the genitive. स्वामित्व या संबंध दिखाना संबंध कारक है। rule — rule living nouns: add -ගේ: ළමයා → ළමයාගේ, අම්මා → අම්මාගේ. non-living nouns: add -ේ (the ending changes, often a → ේ): ගම → ගමේ, ගස → ගසේ, පාසල → පාසලේ. question: කාගේද? (whose?). the genitive word comes before the noun it describes: ළමයාගේ පොත (the child’s book). in hindi it comes before too: बच्चे की किताब. # pronoun genitive english hindi 1 මම mama මගේ mage my मेरा 2 අපි api අපේ ape our हमारा 3 ඔබ oba ඔබේ obe your आपका 4 ඔහු ohu ඔහුගේ ohuge his उसका 5 ඇය aeya ඇයගේ aeyage her उसकी 6 ඔවුන් owun ඔවුන්ගේ owunge their उनका # sinhala english hindi 1 ළමයාගේ පොත lamayaage potha the child’s book बच्चे की किताब 2 ගුරුවරයාගේ නම guruwarayaage nama the teacher’s name शिक्षक का नाम 3 අම්මාගේ ගෙදර ammaage gedara mother’s house माँ का घर 4 ගමේ පාසල game paasala the village school गाँव का स्कूल 5 ගසේ කොළ gase kola the leaves of the tree पेड़ के पत्ते 6 මගේ යාළුවා mage yaaluwaa my friend मेरा दोस्त 7 ඔබේ නම මොකක්ද? obe nama mokakda what is your name? आपका नाम क्या है? 8 අපේ රට ශ්රී ලංකාව. ape rata shrii lankaawa our country is sri lanka. हमारा देश श्रीलंका है। 9 ඔවුන්ගේ ගෙදර ලොකුයි. owunge gedara lokuyi their house is big. उनका घर बड़ा है। 10 ඔහුගේ අම්මා ගුරුවරියක්. ohuge ammaa guruwariyak his mother is a teacher. उसकी माँ शिक्षिका है। 11 ඇයගේ පොත අළුත්. aeyage potha alut her book is new. उसकी किताब नई है। 12 පාසලේ ගේට්ටුව paasale gettuwa the school gate स्कूल का फाटक

13.3 word bank (වචන මාලාව) # sinhala english hindi 1 පඤ්චමී panchamii ablative case अपादान कारक 2 ෂෂ්ඨී shashtii genitive case सम्बन्ध कारक 3 ඉල්ලනවා illanawaa asks for, requests माँगता है 4 අහනවා ahanawaa asks (a question) पूछता है 5 පිටත් වෙනවා pitath wenawaa leaves, departs निकलता है 6 වැටෙනවා waetenawaa falls गिरता है 7 බය baya fear डर 8 අයිතිය ayithiya ownership स्वामित्व 9 ගේට්ටුව gettuwa gate फाटक 10 ප්රශ්නය prashnaya question प्रश्न

13.4 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. ablative (from): non-living -ෙන්; living -ගෙන්. question කොහෙන්ද / කාගෙන්ද. 2. instrumental and ablative look alike for things; decide by meaning. 3. genitive (of): living -ගේ; non-living -ේ. question කාගේද. 4. genitive comes before the noun: ළමයාගේ පොත. 5. pronouns: මගේ, අපේ, ඔබේ, ඔහුගේ, ඇයගේ, ඔවුන්ගේ.

13.6 answer key (පිළිතුරු) q answer rule to remember 1 (a) ගමෙන් (b) පාසලෙන් (c) ගුරුවරයාගෙන් (d) අම්මාගෙන් 13.1 2 non-living takes -ෙන්; living takes -ගෙන් 13.1 3 ඔහු පාසලෙන් ආවා. 13.1 4 (a) ළමයාගේ (b) ගුරුවරයාගේ (c) ගමේ (d) ගසේ 13.2 5 මගේ, අපේ, ඔබේ, ඔහුගේ, ඇයගේ, ඔවුන්ගේ 13.2 6 ළමයාගේ පොත; ගමේ පාසල 13.2 7 මම ගුරුවරයාගෙන් ඉගෙන ගත්තා. 13.1 8 ඔවුන්ගේ ගෙදර ලොකුයි. 13.2 9 the child asked his mother for milk. 13.1 10 leaves fall from the tree. 13.1 tip — coming next lesson 14: locative (සප්තමී) and vocative (ආලපන). “in, on, at” and “o …!”.

lesson 14 lesson 14: locative and vocative cases සප්තමී සහ ආලපන විභක්ති अधिकरण और सम्बोधन कारक key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. the locative case (සප්තමී): in, on, at 2. spoken -ේ and written -ෙහි 3. place words: උඩ, යට, තුළ, ළඟ 4. the vocative case (ආලපන): calling people

14.1 the locative case (සප්තමී) – “in, on, at” ක්රියාව සිදුවන ස්ථානය ආධාරය ය. kriyaawa sidduwana sthaanaya aadhaaraya ya. the place where an action happens is the locative. जहाँ क्रिया होती है वह स्थान अधिकरण है। rule — rule spoken: the ending -ේ (as in the genitive): ගම → ගමේ, පාසල → පාසලේ, පොත → පොතේ. written: the ending -ෙහි: ගමෙහි, පාසලෙහි, නිවසෙහි. question: කොහෙද? (where?). place names such as කොළඹ often take no ending: කොළඹ වැඩ කරනවා. for living nouns, use ළඟ (near, with): ළමයා ළඟ. # non-living noun locative (spoken) written 1 ගම gama ගමේ game ගමෙහි gamehi 2 පාසල paasala පාසලේ paasale පාසලෙහි paasalehi 3 පොත potha පොතේ pothe පොතෙහි pothehi 4 පන්තිය panthiya පන්තියේ panthiye පන්තියෙහි panthiyehi 5 කුස්සිය kussiya කුස්සියේ kussiye කුස්සියෙහි kussiyehi 6 ගෙවත්ත gewaththa ගෙවත්තේ gewaththe ගෙවත්තෙහි gewaththehi place words (පශ්චාත් නිපාත) can be added to give a more exact place. they come after the noun: # sinhala english example hindi 1 උඩ / මත uda / matha on, above මේසය උඩ mesaya uda मेज़ पर 2 යට yata under ඇඳ යට aeda yata पलंग के नीचे 3 තුළ / ඇතුළේ thula / aethule inside බෑගය තුළ baegaya thula बैग के अंदर 4 ළඟ langa near, with ගුරුවරයා ළඟ guruwarayaa langa शिक्षक के पास 5 ඉදිරියේ / ඉස්සරහා idiriye / issarahaa in front of ගෙදර ඉස්සරහා gedara issarahaa घर के सामने 6 පිටුපස / පස්සේ pitupasa / passe behind ගෙදර පිටුපස gedara pitupasa घर के पीछे # sinhala english hindi 1 ළමයා පාසලේ ඉන්නවා. lamayaa paasale innawaa the child is at school. बच्चा स्कूल में है। 2 පොත මේසය උඩ තියෙනවා. potha mesaya uda thiyenawaa the book is on the table. किताब मेज़ पर है। 3 මල් ගෙවත්තේ තියෙනවා. mal gewaththe thiyenawaa there are flowers in the garden. बगीचे में फूल हैं। 4 අම්මා කුස්සියේ ඉන්නවා. ammaa kussiye innawaa mother is in the kitchen. माँ रसोई में है। 5 අපි ගමේ ඉපදුණා. api game ipadunaa we were born in the village. हम गाँव में पैदा हुए। 6 ඔහු කොළඹ වැඩ කරනවා. ohu kolaba wae karanawaa he works in colombo. वह कोलंबो में काम करता है। 7 කුරුල්ලා ගසේ ඉන්නවා. kurullaa gase innawaa the bird is in the tree. चिड़िया पेड़ पर है। 8 මම පන්තියේ ඉන්නවා. mama panthiye innawaa i am in the class. मैं कक्षा में हूँ। 9 පොත බෑගය තුළ තියෙනවා. potha baegaya thula thiyenawaa the book is inside the bag. किताब बैग के अंदर है। 10 මල් බඳුනේ තියෙනවා. mal bandune thiyenawaa the flowers are in the vase. फूल गुलदान में हैं। 11 මම ගෙදර ඉන්නවා. mama gedara innawaa i am at home. मैं घर पर हूँ। 12 මගේ ළඟ පොතක් තියෙනවා. mage langa pothak thiyenawaa i have a book (with me). मेरे पास एक किताब है।

14.2 the vocative case (ආලපන) – calling කෙනෙකු කතා කර අමතන විට යෙදෙන්නේ ආලපන විභක්තියයි. kenekuta kathaa kara amathana wita yedenne aalapana wibhakthiyayi. the vocative is used when we call or address someone. किसी को पुकारते समय सम्बोधन कारक का प्रयोग होता है। rule — rule the final vowel changes: -ා → -ේ (අම්මා → අම්මේ, තාත්තා → තාත්තේ, අක්කා → අක්කේ). plural calling uses -නේ: ළමයි → ළමයිනේ, යාළුවෝ → යාළුවනේ. respectful: -නි: ගුරුතුමා → ගුරුතුමනි. it usually comes first in the sentence, with a comma, and ends in ! or ?. # sinhala english hindi 1 අම්මේ, මෙහෙ එන්න! ammee, mehe enna mother, come here! माँ, यहाँ आओ! 2 තාත්තේ, මට බඩගිනියි. thaaththee, mata badaginiyi father, i am hungry. पिताजी, मुझे भूख लगी है। 3 අයියේ, කොහෙද යන්නේ? ayyee, kohedha yanne brother, where are you going? भैया, कहाँ जा रहे हो? 4 අක්කේ, මේක බලන්න. akkee, meeka balanna sister, look at this. दीदी, इसे देखो। 5 මල්ලී, ඉක්මනට එන්න. malli, ikmanata enna younger brother, come quickly. छोटे भाई, जल्दी आओ। 6 ගුරුතුමනි, මට පැහැදිලි කරන්න. gurutumani, mata paehaedili karanna sir, please explain to me. गुरुजी, कृपया मुझे समझाइए। 7 යාළුවනේ, අපි යමු! yaaluwanee, api yamu friends, let us go! दोस्तो, चलो! 8 ළමයිනේ, නිශ්ශබ්දව ඉන්න. lamayinee, nishshabdawa inna children, be quiet. बच्चो, चुप रहो। 9 දෙවියනේ! deviyanee o god! (surprise) हे भगवान! 10 නංගී, මෙහෙ එන්න. nangii, mehe enna younger sister, come here. छोटी बहन, यहाँ आओ।

lesson 15 lesson 15: all cases together: tables and workshop සියලු විභක්ති එකට सभी कारक: तालिकाएँ और अभ्यास key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. case endings for living and non-living nouns 2. full tables: ළමයා, ගුරුවරයා, අම්මා, පොත, ගම 3. plural case endings 4. a workshop: find the case, supply the ending
15.1  The Case Endings at a Glance

15.1 the case endings at a glance # case living nouns non-living nouns example 1 nominative no ending no ending ළමයා, පොත 2 accusative -ව no ending ළමයාව; පොත 3 instrumental විසින් (agent) -ෙන් / -ින් ළමයා විසින්; පෑනෙන් 4 dative -ට -ට ළමයාට; ගමට 5 ablative -ගෙන් -ෙන් / -ින් ළමයාගෙන්; ගමෙන් 6 genitive -ගේ -ේ ළමයාගේ; ගමේ 7 locative ළඟ -ේ (written -ෙහි) ළමයා ළඟ; ගමේ 8 vocative -ේ / -නි / -නේ — අම්මේ, ගුරුතුමනි tip — plural of non-living nouns in the plural, non-living nouns use -වල for several cases: පොත්වල (of / in the books), පොත්වලට (to), පොත්වලින් (from / by). living plurals use the base form (ළමයින්) and then the singular endings: ළමයින්ට, ළමයින්ගේ, ළමයින්ගෙන්.

15.6 quick revision (පුනරීක්ෂණය) key idea — remember these points 1. eight cases; living and non-living nouns take different endings. 2. living: -ව, විසින්, -ට, -ගෙන්, -ගේ, ළඟ. non-living: no ending, -ෙන්, -ට, -ෙන්, -ේ, -ේ. 3. plural non-living: -වල, -වලට, -වලින්. plural living: base ළමයින් + ending. 4. to find a case, ask: කවුද, කාවද, කුමකින්ද, කාටද, කොහෙන්ද, කාගේද, කොහෙද.

lesson 16 lesson 16: verbs ක්රියා පද क्रिया key idea — what you will learn in this lesson 1. what a verb (ක්රියා පදය) is, and the root (ධාතුව) 2. the dictionary form in -නවා 3. the main forms of one verb 4. twenty everyday verbs 5. verbs with and without an object 6. “doing” and “happening” verbs 7. verbs made with කරනවා and වෙනවා
16.1  What Is a Verb?  (ක්‍රියා පදය යනු කුමක්ද?)

16.1 what is a verb? (ක්රියා පදය යනු කුමක්ද?) යමක් කිරීම හෝ සිදුවීම දක්වන පදය ක්රියා පදය නම් වේ. yamak kiriima ho siduwiima dakwana padaya kriyaa padaya nam we. a verb is a word that shows doing or happening. जो शब्द किसी काम का करना या होना बताए, वह क्रिया है। every verb has a root (ධාතුව, hindi धातु) that carries the meaning, and an ending that shows time and person. the form you find in a dictionary ends in -නවා: බලනවා (to look), යනවා (to go). take away -නවා and you have the stem: බල-, ය-. බල- stem → + නවා ending → බලනවා looks / look
16.2  The Main Forms of One Verb

16.2 the main forms of one verb one verb gives many forms. learn them for බලනවා now; the same pattern serves hundreds of verbs. form sinhala english hindi present (spoken) බලනවා balanawaa look(s), is looking देखता है past (spoken) බැලුවා baeluwaa looked देखा infinitive බලන්න balanna to look देखना “having done” form බලලා balalaa having looked देखकर present describing form බලන balana (the one) who looks देखने वाला past describing form බැලූ baeluu (the one) who looked देखा हुआ verbal noun බැලීම baeliima looking (the act) देखना (संज्ञा) written present, he/she බලයි balayi looks देखता है written past, he බැලුවේය baeluweeya looked देखा
